governing_thought: A cross-entity exploratory meeting should be approved within 4 weeks to assess whether co-sponsoring or co-designing the AI Agent Economy Competition—a controlled on-chain testbed studying AI behavior under real incentives—can generate reusable research assets (auditable datasets, institution-design frameworks) that inform SGE's AI-in-education roadmap, Startale/Soneium's trust-infrastructure positioning, and Sony Group's frontier AI governance stance, with participation tiers (observer to co-designer) enabling low-commitment entry and clear exit gates.
key_claims: Current pain: The industry lacks empirical testbeds to study how AI agents behave under real economic incentives; most simulations use synthetic rewards, limiting generalizability and leaving emergent risks (collusion, manipulation) poorly understood.

Solution validity: A private-chain competition with auditable logs, human-in-the-loop rule design, and explicit governance boundaries uniquely combines incentive realism, reproducibility, and safety controls—directly aligned with SGE's learner-centered evaluation priorities and Startale/Soneium's trust-infrastructure mission.

Feasibility: Nyx Foundation has demonstrated Ethereum security credibility (17 vulnerabilities reported in Fusaka audit, #1 by report count); modular participation tiers and staged pilot phases minimize operational burden for each entity; September 2025 target is internal and adjustable.

Risk handling: Private chain (no public token, no speculation), sandbox isolation with kill-switches, brand/legal review gates, and post-hoc analysis of harmful behaviors convert risk into research data—not uncontrolled exposure.
supporting_evidence_needed: Pilot/prototype metrics: throughput, stability, and sandbox security results from internal test runs (before any public launch commitment).
Landscape comparison: citation-backed survey of existing AI-agent economic experiments/competitions with meaningful incentives to validate differentiation claims.
Benchmark participation data: reference Google ADK Hackathon (10,400+ participants, 477 projects) and ARC Prize ($1M) as scale/prize comparables.
SGE alignment artifacts: quotes or signals from Isozu's 2025 interview on AI evaluation redesign (real-time, multi-dimensional, learner-centered) to anchor educational relevance.
Legal/regulatory memo: confirm Japanese prize competition treatment for private-chain tokens; outline compliance stance for participant terms.
Third-party security review plan: timeline and scope for external audit of agent sandbox and validator logic before September 2025.

alternatives_considered.governing_thought: Sony Group / SGE should pursue internal R&D or established academic partnerships (e.g., Santa Fe Institute, university labs) to study AI-agent economics, avoiding the operational complexity and brand exposure of a public competition.
tradeoffs: Lower brand/regulatory risk and simpler governance, but limited incentive realism (synthetic rewards) and less external validity.
Smaller public dataset contribution and reduced ecosystem/community engagement; misses spectator-experience and recruitment benefits.
May replicate rather than complement existing simulation research; opportunity cost if competitors define the benchmark first.

alternatives_considered.governing_thought: Sony Group / SGE should observe the first competition as a spectator or advisor (no sponsorship commitment), evaluate the pilot outcomes, and decide on deeper involvement only after reviewing published results and datasets.
tradeoffs: Minimal upfront commitment and brand exposure; clear exit if pilot fails or governance concerns arise.
Reduced influence on rule design, research agenda, and data access; less strategic positioning at the AI-agent research frontier.
Delayed strategic benefit: if the competition succeeds, late entry may yield less favorable partnership terms or brand positioning.
